0.title: First Steps in Following Jesus
0.overview:
If you have recently put your trust in Jesus Christ, welcome to the family of God. This is the most important decision you will ever make, and it is the beginning of a new life. You may have many questions. What exactly happened to me? How can I be sure I am saved? How do I pray? Where do I start reading the Bible? Do I need to go to church? What about baptism? How do I deal with sin?

This short study answers those questions simply. It is written for new Christians, but it may also help anyone who wants to be sure of the basics. Each unit points to other studies in this app where you can go deeper when you are ready.

Jesus said, I came that they may have life and have it abundantly (John 10:10). The Christian life is not a list of rules but a relationship with God through Jesus, by the Holy Spirit. It begins with grace, continues by grace and ends in glory.

Five units: (1) What Happened When You Believed; (2) Sure of Your Salvation; (3) Prayer and the Bible; (4) You Belong: Church and Baptism; (5) Living the New Life.

1.title: What Happened When You Believed
1.overview:
When you trusted in Jesus, several wonderful things happened, all at once, whether you felt them or not.

You were forgiven. Every sin you have ever committed, past, present and future, was paid for by Jesus on the cross. In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of his grace (Eph 1:7). God no longer counts your sins against you.

You were made right with God. God declared you righteous, not because of anything you did, but because of what Jesus did. Therefore, since we have been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ (Rom 5:1). You are at peace with God.

You were born again. God gave you new life by his Spirit. Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come (2 Cor 5:17). You are not just a better version of your old self; you are a new person.

You became God's child. But to all who did receive him, who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God (John 1:12). God is now your Father. You belong to his family.

The Holy Spirit came to live in you. God's Spirit lives in every believer, helping you understand the Bible, pray, fight sin and grow (Rom 8:9).

It was all grace. For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast (Eph 2:8-9). You did not earn any of this. God gave it freely, because he loves you.
1.theology:
Faith and repentance: Becoming a Christian involves turning from sin (repentance) and trusting in Jesus (faith). These go together like two sides of a coin. Both continue for the rest of your life.

Feelings: Some people feel great joy when they become Christians; others feel very little. Your salvation does not depend on your feelings but on what God has done and promised.

Going deeper: The Grace of God and The Person and Work of Christ studies explain these truths more fully.
1.examples:
Then: A jailer in Philippi, terrified after an earthquake, asked Paul and Silas, Sirs, what must I do to be saved? They answered, Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household. That same night he was baptised, and he rejoiced along with his entire household that he had believed in God (Acts 16:30-34).

Now: A young man becomes a Christian after attending a church course. He does not feel very different at first, and worries that it did not work. An older Christian shows him 2 Corinthians 5:17 and John 1:12. These things are true because God says so, not because he feels them. Over the following months, he notices real changes in his desires and habits.

A simple test: Can you explain in your own words what happened when you trusted in Jesus?

verseByVerse.quote: But to all who did receive him, who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God, who were born, not of blood nor of the will of the flesh nor of the will of man, but of God. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Everyone who receives Jesus and believes in his name is given the right to become God's child. This new birth is not by human effort or family background, but by God. Being a Christian means being adopted into God's family.

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore, since we have been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. Through him we have also obtained access by faith into this grace in which we stand, and we rejoice in hope of the glory of God. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Because we are justified by faith, we have peace with God through Jesus. We have access by faith into God's grace, and we rejoice in the hope of his glory. Peace with God, access to God and hope in God: these belong to every believer.

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Anyone in Christ is a new creation. The old life has gone, and the new has come. This does not mean you will never struggle again. It means God has begun a new work in you that he will complete.

verseByVerse.quote: For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Salvation is by grace, through faith, not by works. It is God's gift, so no one can boast. But Paul continues: we are God's workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works. We are not saved by good works, but we are saved for them.

1.reflection:
Which of the things that happened when you believed means most to you? Why?

Why is it important that salvation is a gift, not something we earn?

How would you explain to a friend what it means to become a Christian?

Thank God for what he did for you when you believed.

2.title: Sure of Your Salvation
2.overview:
Many new Christians wonder whether they are really saved, especially when they sin again or do not feel close to God. God wants you to be sure.

God wants you to know. I write these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life (1 John 5:13). John did not write so that you would hope or guess, but so that you would know.

Based on God's promise. Your assurance rests on what God has said. And this is the testimony, that God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life (1 John 5:11-12). If you have trusted in Jesus, you have the Son, and you have life.

Held by Jesus. Jesus said, My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me. I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand (John 10:27-28). Your security depends not on how tightly you hold Jesus, but on how tightly he holds you.

God finishes what he starts. And I am sure of this, that he who began a good work in you will bring it to completion at the day of Jesus Christ (Phil 1:6). God does not start projects and abandon them.

Nothing can separate you. For I am sure that neither death nor life, nor angels nor rulers, nor things present nor things to come, nor powers, nor height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord (Rom 8:38-39).

When you sin. You will still sin. When you do, you are not lost. Confess it to God, and he will forgive you (1 John 1:9). If anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous (1 John 2:1).
2.theology:
Evidence of new life: While assurance rests on God's promises, John also shows signs of new life: believing in Jesus, loving other Christians, wanting to obey God and turning from sin. These signs grow over time and strengthen assurance.

Persevering: True believers will keep trusting Christ to the end, not because they are strong, but because God keeps them. Those who permanently walk away show they never truly belonged (1 John 2:19). If you are worried about this, that worry itself is often a sign of real faith.

Going deeper: The Assurance of Salvation study explains this more fully.
2.examples:
Then: Peter denied Jesus three times, the worst failure of his life. Yet Jesus had prayed for him, and after the resurrection Jesus restored him (Luke 22:32; John 21:15-19). Peter's salvation did not depend on his performance but on Christ's faithfulness.

Now: A new Christian loses her temper badly with her sister and wonders whether she was ever really saved. She reads 1 John 1:9 and 2:1, confesses her sin to God, and apologises to her sister. She learns that the Christian life is not about never falling, but about always coming back.

A simple test: On what do you base your assurance of salvation: your feelings, your performance or God's promise?

verseByVerse.quote: And this is the testimony, that God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life. I write these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God's testimony is that he has given eternal life, and that life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life. John wrote so that believers would know they have eternal life. Assurance is not arrogance; it is taking God at his word.

verseByVerse.quote: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me. I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand. My Father, who has given them to me, is greater than all, and no one is able to snatch them out of the Father's hand. I and the Father are one." (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus' sheep hear his voice and follow him. He gives them eternal life, and no one can snatch them out of his hand or his Father's hand. Your security rests in the hands of the Father and the Son.

verseByVerse.quote: I thank my God in all my remembrance of you, always in every prayer of mine for you all making my prayer with joy, because of your partnership in the gospel from the first day until now. And I am sure of this, that he who began a good work in you will bring it to completion at the day of Jesus Christ. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul thanks God for the Philippians and is confident that God, who began a good work in them, will complete it at the day of Christ. Your salvation is God's work from beginning to end, and he will finish it.

verseByVerse.quote: My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you may not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous. He is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only but also for the sins of the whole world. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: We all sin, and if we confess our sins, God is faithful and just to forgive us (1 John 1:9). If anyone sins, we have an advocate, Jesus Christ the righteous, who is the propitiation for our sins. Failure is not final for the believer.

2.reflection:
Why does God want you to be sure of your salvation?

What is the difference between assurance based on feelings and assurance based on God's promises?

What should you do when you sin?

Memorise John 10:27-28 or 1 John 5:13 this week.

3.title: Prayer and the Bible
3.overview:
Every relationship grows through communication. In prayer, you speak to God. In the Bible, God speaks to you.

Prayer. Prayer is simply talking to God as your Father. You do not need special words. Jesus gave his disciples a pattern: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil (Matt 6:9-13). This prayer covers praise, God's purposes, our needs, forgiveness and protection.

Pray about everything. Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God (Phil 4:6). Nothing is too big or too small to bring to God.

The Bible. The Bible is God's word to you. All Scripture is breathed out by God and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness (2 Tim 3:16). It is a lamp for your path (Ps 119:105) and food for your soul. Like newborn infants, long for the pure spiritual milk, that by it you may grow up into salvation (1 Pet 2:2).

Where to start. A good place to begin is one of the Gospels, such as Mark or John, to get to know Jesus. Then read Acts, and some of the shorter letters like Philippians or 1 John. Read the Psalms for prayer. Read a little each day, perhaps a chapter, and ask: What does this show me about God? About Jesus? About myself? What should I believe or do?

A daily habit. Try to set aside a regular time each day, even fifteen minutes, to read the Bible and pray. Many find the morning best. It is not a duty to earn God's favour, but a time to enjoy him.
3.theology:
Praying in Jesus' name: We pray to the Father, through Jesus, by the Holy Spirit. Praying in Jesus' name means coming to God on the basis of what Jesus has done, not our own goodness (John 14:13).

Understanding Scripture: Some parts of the Bible are hard to understand. That is normal. Ask questions, use a good study Bible or the commentaries in this app, and talk with mature Christians.

Going deeper: The Prayer, Spiritual Disciplines and Big Story of the Bible studies will help you grow in these areas.
3.examples:
Then: Jesus himself made time to pray. And rising very early in the morning, while it was still dark, he departed and went out to a desolate place, and there he prayed (Mark 1:35). If Jesus needed time alone with the Father, so do we.

Now: A new Christian has never read the Bible. He starts reading Mark's Gospel, one chapter each morning, and writes down one thing he learns about Jesus each day. After sixteen days, he has finished his first book of the Bible and knows Jesus far better.

A simple test: When and where will you read the Bible and pray tomorrow?

verseByVerse.quote: "And when you pray, you must not be like the hypocrites. For they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and at the street corners, that they may be seen by others. Truly, I say to you, they have received their reward. But when you pray, go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret. And your Father who sees in secret will reward you. "And when you pray, do not heap up empty phrases as the Gentiles do, for they think that they will be heard for their many words. Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him. Pray then like this: "Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Jesus teaches that prayer should be sincere, not for show, and not full of empty words. Our Father knows what we need before we ask. Then he gives a pattern prayer: God's name, God's kingdom, God's will, our bread, our forgiveness, our protection. It is a model for all our prayers.

verseByVerse.quote: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: God's word is a lamp to our feet and a light to our path. It does not always show the whole road ahead, but it shows the next step. Reading the Bible daily gives light for daily decisions.

verseByVerse.quote: But as for you, continue in what you have learned and have firmly believed, knowing from whom you learned it and how from childhood you have been acquainted with the sacred writings, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus. All Scripture is breathed out by God and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness, that the man of God may be complete, equipped for every good work. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul reminds Timothy that he learned the Scriptures from childhood, and that they make us wise for salvation through faith in Christ. All Scripture is breathed out by God and equips us for every good work. The Bible is God's own word, given for our growth.

verseByVerse.quote: So put away all malice and all deceit and hypocrisy and envy and all slander. Like newborn infants, long for the pure spiritual milk, that by it you may grow up into salvation— if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is good. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Peter tells new believers to put away sins like malice and envy, and to long for the pure spiritual milk of God's word, like newborn babies. By it they will grow. If you have tasted that the Lord is good, you will want more.

3.reflection:
What does the Lord's Prayer teach you about how to pray?

Which book of the Bible will you start reading this week?

When is the best time in your day to read and pray?

Pray through the Lord's Prayer slowly, putting each line in your own words.

4.title: You Belong: Church and Baptism
4.overview:
When you became a Christian, you joined a family. God never intended his children to live alone.

The church. The church is not a building but God's people. You are now part of the body of Christ: Now you are the body of Christ and individually members of it (1 Cor 12:27). You need other Christians, and they need you.

Find a good church. Look for a church where the Bible is faithfully taught, Jesus is at the centre, the gospel is clear and people genuinely care for one another. Go regularly. Get to know people. Ask about membership.

Do not go it alone. And let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works, not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another (Heb 10:24-25). Christians who stay away from church usually struggle to grow.

Baptism. Jesus commanded his followers to be baptised (Matt 28:19). Baptism is a public sign that you belong to Jesus. It pictures your sins washed away and your union with Christ in his death and resurrection (Rom 6:3-4). It does not save you, but it is an important step of obedience. In the New Testament, people were baptised soon after believing: So those who received his word were baptized (Acts 2:41). If you have not been baptised as a believer, speak to a pastor about it.

The Lord's Supper. Jesus also gave his church a meal to remember him: bread and wine, representing his body and blood (1 Cor 11:23-26). Baptised believers share in it regularly, remembering his death and being strengthened by him.

Serving. Every Christian has gifts to serve others in the church (1 Pet 4:10). Look for ways to help, however small.
4.theology:
Why church matters: God has chosen to work through his church: through preaching, baptism, the Lord's Supper, fellowship and the care of elders. These are called the means of grace.

Baptism and faith: Christians differ over whether infants should be baptised. The New Testament examples show baptism following a profession of faith, and that is the practice to follow. The Church and Covenant Theology studies explain this more fully.

Going deeper: The Church and the Worship and the Lord's Day studies cover these topics in more detail.
4.examples:
Then: On the day of Pentecost, about three thousand people believed. They were baptised, and they devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers (Acts 2:42). From the start, believers belonged to a church.

Now: A woman who came to faith through an online video is nervous about going to church. A friend offers to go with her. She finds a warm welcome, joins a small group and is baptised a few months later. She says that belonging to the church has helped her grow more than anything else.

A simple test: Have you found a church family? If not, what is your next step?

verseByVerse.quote: And Peter said to them, "Repent and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For the promise is for you and for your children and for all who are far off, everyone whom the Lord our God calls to himself." And with many other words he bore witness and continued to exhort them, saying, "Save yourselves from this crooked generation." So those who received his word were baptized, and there were added that day about three thousand souls. And they devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Peter called the crowd to repent and be baptised in Jesus' name. Those who received his word were baptised, about three thousand. Then they devoted themselves to teaching, fellowship, the breaking of bread and prayer. Belief, baptism and belonging went together.

verseByVerse.quote: Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for he who promised is faithful. And let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works, not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day drawing near. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Christians are to hold fast their hope, encourage one another to love and good works, and not neglect meeting together. We need each other to keep going. Church is not optional for those who want to grow.

verseByVerse.quote: Do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? We were buried therefore with him by baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Baptism pictures our union with Christ. We were buried with him and raised to walk in new life. Every time you remember your baptism, you remember that your old life died with Christ and your new life belongs to him.

verseByVerse.quote: For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so it is with Christ. For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body—Jews or Greeks, slaves or free—and all were made to drink of one Spirit. For the body does not consist of one member but of many. If the foot should say, "Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body," that would not make it any less a part of the body. And if the ear should say, "Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body," that would not make it any less a part of the body. If the whole body were an eye, where would be the sense of hearing? If the whole body were an ear, where would be the sense of smell? But as it is, God arranged the members in the body, each one of them, as he chose. If all were a single member, where would the body be? As it is, there are many parts, yet one body. The eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you," nor again the head to the feet, "I have no need of you." On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable, and on those parts of the body that we think less honorable we bestow the greater honor, and our unpresentable parts are treated with greater modesty, which our more presentable parts do not require. But God has so composed the body, giving greater honor to the part that lacked it, that there may be no division in the body, but that the members may have the same care for one another. If one member suffers, all suffer together; if one member is honored, all rejoice together. Now you are the body of Christ and individually members of it. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The church is like a body with many parts. Every part matters. The eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you." You have a place in Christ's body, and the body needs you.

4.reflection:
Why do you need other Christians, and why do they need you?

What should you look for in a church?

Have you been baptised as a believer? If not, what is your next step?

How could you begin serving in your church?

5.title: Living the New Life
5.overview:
Keep walking with Jesus. Therefore, as you received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in him, rooted and built up in him and established in the faith, just as you were taught, abounding in thanksgiving (Col 2:6-7). You began by trusting Jesus; you continue the same way.

Fighting sin. You will still face temptation and sin. That is normal. But now you have the Holy Spirit to help you. But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh (Gal 5:16). Some habits may change quickly; others will take time. Do not give up. When you fall, confess and get up again.

Changed priorities. I appeal to you therefore, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship (Rom 12:1). Every part of your life now belongs to God: your time, money, relationships, work and body.

Telling others. You have the best news in the world. You do not need to be an expert to share it. Like the man Jesus healed, you can simply say, One thing I do know, that though I was blind, now I see (John 9:25). Be ready to explain your hope, gently and respectfully (1 Pet 3:15).

Facing hardship. Becoming a Christian does not mean life will be easy. Some new believers face opposition from family or friends. Jesus warned that following him would be costly. But he also promised, I am with you always (Matt 28:20).

Growing. The Christian life is a journey. You will not become mature overnight. But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ (2 Pet 3:18). Keep reading, praying, belonging and obeying, and God will grow you.
5.theology:
Grace and effort: Growing as a Christian involves effort: reading, praying, resisting sin. But it is God who gives the growth. For it is God who works in you, both to will and to work for his good pleasure (Phil 2:13).

Mentors: It is wise for new Christians to have an older, mature Christian of the same sex to meet with, pray with and ask questions.

Going deeper: The Fighting Sin, Evangelism and Christian Suffering studies will help you as you grow.
5.examples:
Then: When Jesus healed a man possessed by demons, the man begged to go with him. Jesus said, Go home to your friends and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and how he has had mercy on you (Mark 5:19). The man went and told people in ten cities, and everyone marvelled.

Now: A new Christian tells her best friend what has happened to her. The friend is sceptical, but notices over the next year how much she has changed: calmer, kinder, more honest. Eventually the friend asks to come to church with her.

A simple test: Who is one person you could tell about what Jesus has done for you?

verseByVerse.quote: Therefore, as you received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in him, rooted and built up in him and established in the faith, just as you were taught, abounding in thanksgiving. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Paul urges believers to keep walking in Christ the way they received him: by faith. They are to be rooted like a tree, built up like a building and established in the faith, overflowing with thanksgiving. The Christian life continues as it began, by trusting Jesus.

verseByVerse.quote: But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh. For the desires of the flesh are against the Spirit, and the desires of the Spirit are against the flesh, for these are opposed to each other, to keep you from doing the things you want to do. But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law. Now the works of the flesh are evident: sexual immorality, impurity, sensuality, idolatry, sorcery, enmity, strife, jealousy, fits of anger, rivalries, dissensions, divisions, envy, drunkenness, orgies, and things like these. I warn you, as I warned you before, that those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God. But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control; against such things there is no law. And those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires. If we live by the Spirit, let us also keep in step with the Spirit. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The desires of the flesh and the Spirit are at war. Walking by the Spirit means not gratifying the flesh. The works of the flesh are obvious, but the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. The Spirit grows this fruit in you.

verseByVerse.quote: As he was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed with demons begged him that he might be with him. And he did not permit him but said to him, "Go home to your friends and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and how he has had mercy on you." And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him, and everyone marveled. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: The healed man wanted to follow Jesus, but Jesus sent him home to tell his friends what the Lord had done. He went and proclaimed it throughout the Decapolis. You do not need training to tell others what Jesus has done for you.

verseByVerse.quote: You therefore, beloved, knowing this beforehand, take care that you are not carried away with the error of lawless people and lose your own stability. But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To him be the glory both now and to the day of eternity. Amen. (ESV)
verseByVerse.commentary: Peter's final words urge believers to beware of error and to grow in the grace and knowledge of the Lord Jesus. Then he gives glory to Christ, now and forever. Growth in grace is lifelong, and its goal is Christ's glory.

5.reflection:
What does it mean to "walk in" Christ as you received him?

What sin or habit do you most need the Spirit's help to overcome?

Who could you tell about what Jesus has done for you?

What is one step you can take this week to grow in your faith?
